name: DraftBridge: From Doc/Docx to Blog Post
author: SiteAuditHub

sections.description:
DraftBridge turns a finished Google Doc, Word file or Markdown file into a ready-to-review WordPress post in one click: no copy-pasting, no broken formatting, no re-uploading images one by one.

Paste a Google Doc link, upload .docx or .md files, or pick Word files already in your Media Library. Click Preview to check the headings, SEO fields and any problems, then click Import now. Posts are saved as drafts for you to review.

Read the step-by-step guide

Ways to import

  • Google Doc links: paste one or more share links (sharing set to “Anyone with the link”).
  • Word (.docx) files: upload from your computer, exported from Word or Google Docs.
  • Markdown (.md) files: notes from Notion, Obsidian or Joplin, a README, or text from ChatGPT or Claude.
  • Media Library: import a .docx that is already on your site. The original file is only read, never changed or removed.
  • Bulk import: up to 20 links or files at once, each with its own result.

Formatting that comes across

  • Title and headings: the doc’s Title (or first Heading 1) becomes the post title; Heading 2-6 become H2-H6.
  • Text formatting: bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, superscript, subscript and links.
  • Quotes: Word’s “Quote”, “Intense Quote” and “Block Text” styles, and Markdown > quotes, become real Quote blocks (<blockquote>), not italic paragraphs.
  • Alignment: centered and right-aligned paragraphs and headings keep their alignment.
  • Lists: bullet and numbered lists, including nested lists.
  • Tables: with header rows and merged cells.
  • Images: uploaded to the Media Library with their alt text and SEO-friendly file names.
  • Image links: put an image URL on its own line (optionally followed by | alt text) and it is downloaded into the Media Library.
  • Picture and table captions: captions added with Word’s References → Insert Caption become the Image or Table block’s caption.
  • Footnotes and endnotes: numbered in the text with the notes at the end of the post, using WordPress’s own Footnotes block on the block editor. Hover or tap a number to read the note in a pop-up.
  • Video embeds: a YouTube, Vimeo, Dailymotion, TED, TikTok, Spotify or SoundCloud link on its own line becomes a playable embed. Links inside a sentence stay links.
  • Text boxes: words inside text boxes (newsletters, brochures, flyers) come across as normal paragraphs.
  • Code blocks (Markdown): fenced code becomes a real Code block, plus horizontal rules as Separator blocks.

SEO and post details

  • SEO fields from the doc: lines like Meta Title:, Meta Description:, Focus Keyword:, Slug:, Category:, Tags: and Excerpt: are filled into Rank Math, Yoast SEO or SEOPress and removed from the post body.
  • FAQ schema: if the doc has an “FAQs” section, FAQPage structured data is added to the page and stays in sync when you edit the FAQs later.
  • Word properties: the Keywords in a Word file (File → Info) become tags, and its Title is used when the doc has no heading to name the post.
  • Markdown front matter: title, slug, excerpt, tags, categories and description fill in the post and SEO fields.
  • Featured image: the first image in the doc, or any image you choose from the Media Library.
  • Categories, tags, author and status: Draft, Pending review, Publish, Schedule for later, or Private.
  • Any content type: Posts, Pages and custom post types.

Safe and in your control

  • Preview before import: see the heading outline, word count, links, quotes, embeds, SEO fields and warnings (missing alt text, no H2, long meta description) before anything is created.
  • Undo an import: “Move it to the trash” on the results screen, for one post or the whole batch. Posts stay restorable from the Trash.
  • Real Gutenberg blocks: every heading, paragraph, quote, list, image, embed and table becomes its own editable block. Classic Editor sites get clean HTML instead.
  • Safe by default: posts are saved as drafts, duplicates are skipped, and user roles are respected (for example, Contributors’ imports are saved as “Pending review”).
  • Choose who can import: administrators pick which user roles may use DraftBridge.
  • Site Health check: Tools → Site Health tells you if the server is missing something imports need (the PHP zip extension, a writable temp folder, matching upload limits).
  • Private by design: documents are read on your own server and deleted straight away. No tracking, no analytics.

Free tools for your imported posts

DraftBridge is made by SiteAuditHub, which also offers free online SEO tools that need no signup. These fit well around an import:

  • Before import: shrink large photos with the free image compressor, so the images DraftBridge uploads to your Media Library load fast.
  • While writing the doc: draft your Meta Title: and Meta Description: lines with the meta tag generator, which shows a live Google preview and length counters.
  • After publishing: run the SEO analyzer on the live post to check the title, headings, image alt text and schema.

External services

DraftBridge connects to outside services only when you ask it to import something:

Google Docs (docs.google.com): when you paste a Google Doc link and click Preview or Import, DraftBridge downloads Google’s own “.docx” export of that document. Only the document ID from your link is sent, as part of the download address. No data about your site or users is sent.
Google Terms of Service: https://policies.google.com/terms
Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Google Drive (drive.google.com): only if your document contains a Google Drive image link. DraftBridge downloads that image into your Media Library. Only the file ID from the link is sent. The same Google terms and privacy policy apply.

Image links in your document: if your document contains an image URL on its own line (or a Markdown image with a full https:// address), DraftBridge downloads the image from that address into your Media Library. The request goes only to the website in the link you wrote; its own terms and privacy policy apply.

Video and audio embeds: when a YouTube, Vimeo or similar link becomes an embed, DraftBridge only saves the link in the post. As with any embed you add yourself, WordPress asks that site for the player when the post is shown, and the visitor’s browser loads the player from it. That site’s own terms and privacy policy apply.

DraftBridge does not track you, send analytics, or contact any server of its own.

Review and suggestion links: the DraftBridge screen and the review reminder link to WordPress.org and to the SiteAuditHub feedback page (siteaudithub.com). These pages open only when you click a link, and the plugin sends no data about you or your site. Anything you enter on those pages is covered by that site’s own terms and privacy policy.

The review reminder keeps its dates and simple click totals in your own WordPress database. They contain no personal information, are never sent anywhere, and can be seen under Tools → Site Health → Info.

sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin from Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, or install it from the plugin directory.
  2. Activate DraftBridge.
  3. Go to DraftBridge in the admin menu.
  4. For Google Docs, set the document’s sharing to “Anyone with the link” (Viewer) and paste the link. Or upload .docx or .md files, or choose .docx files from your Media Library.
sections.faq:
Why do my headings import as normal text?

DraftBridge reads the paragraph style, not the font size. In Google Docs, choose “Heading 2”, “Heading 3” and so on from the style dropdown (“Normal text”). Text that is only bold and large imports as a paragraph.

Are footnotes and endnotes imported?

Yes. Footnotes and endnotes are numbered in reading order (1, 2, 3…) and listed under a “Notes” heading at the end of the post. With the block editor on WordPress 6.3 or newer they use the core Footnotes block; on the Classic Editor or older WordPress versions a plain numbered list is added instead. To change or remove the “Notes” heading, use the draftbridge_notes_heading filter. To turn off the hover pop-ups: add_filter( 'draftbridge_note_popups', '__return_false' );

How are image captions detected?

A caption counts when it was added with Word’s Insert Caption (the “Caption” style or a caption number field), placed directly above or below the picture or table. Plain text under a picture that isn’t styled as a caption stays a normal paragraph.

Why does my Google Doc link fail?

Google only allows the download when the doc’s sharing is set to “Anyone with the link”. Private docs send back a sign-in page, and DraftBridge will tell you when that happens. “Publish to the web” links cannot be used. Use the normal share link instead.

Which SEO plugins are supported?

Rank Math, Yoast SEO and SEOPress. With All in One SEO or no SEO plugin, the SEO lines are shown in the preview but not saved.

Why did my quote import as an italic paragraph?

Update to 1.2.0. Paragraphs in Word’s “Quote”, “Intense Quote” or “Block Text” style (or a style based on them) now become a Quote block. Google Docs has no quote style, so an indented paragraph from Google Docs stays a normal paragraph.

Can I import Markdown files?

Yes. Upload a .md or .markdown file. Headings, bold, italic, links, nested lists, quotes, tables and fenced code blocks are supported. The first # Heading becomes the post title, and front matter (title, slug, excerpt, tags, categories, description) fills in the post. Images need a full https:// address; relative paths like images/photo.jpg are listed in the preview so you can add them yourself.

How do I turn a YouTube link into a video?

Put the link on its own line. It becomes an embed on import. A link inside a sentence stays a normal link. You can switch this off under “Formatting and SEO options”.

Can I undo an import?

Yes. The results screen has “Move it to the trash” for each post and an “Undo this import” link for a batch. Posts can be restored from the Trash, and their images stay in the Media Library.

Can I limit who uses DraftBridge?

Yes. Administrators see “Settings: who can use DraftBridge” at the bottom of the DraftBridge screen. Administrators can always use it.

Why will my file not import?

Go to Tools → Site Health → Status. DraftBridge adds a check there for the usual causes: a missing PHP zip extension, a temporary folder that is not writable, or upload limits that don’t match.

Is my document stored anywhere?

No. Documents are downloaded or uploaded to a temporary folder on your own server, read, and deleted straight away. Files kept between Preview and Import are deleted after import or within a few hours.

Can I import pages or custom post types?

Yes, choose it under “Import as”. Every public content type you are allowed to create is listed.

Do the SiteAuditHub tools send my documents anywhere?

No. The plugin never contacts siteaudithub.com on its own. The free tools on siteaudithub.com are separate web pages that you open yourself, and only when you choose to use them.
sections.changelog:
1.2.1

  • Fix: sites could stop with a critical error after updating to 1.2.0 because the Markdown file was missing from the release. Please update.
  • Improved: if a plugin file is ever missing, DraftBridge now turns itself off and shows a notice instead of stopping the site.
  • Fix: the Media Library option is checked on the server too, not only hidden on the screen.
  • Fix: choosing a schedule date in the past now saves a draft instead of publishing straight away.
  • Fix: clearer message when All in One SEO is active.
  • Improved: very large parts inside a .docx are skipped safely instead of using up the server’s memory.

1.2.0

  • New: Word’s “Quote”, “Intense Quote” and “Block Text” styles become real Quote blocks instead of italic paragraphs.
  • New: centered and right-aligned paragraphs and headings keep their alignment. Underline is kept.
  • New: Markdown (.md) import, with front matter, tables, quotes and code blocks.
  • New: import .docx files that are already in your Media Library.
  • New: a YouTube, Vimeo, TikTok, Spotify or SoundCloud link on its own line becomes an embed.
  • New: the text inside text boxes is imported (newsletters, brochures, flyers).
  • New: Word’s Keywords (File → Info) become tags; Word’s Title names the post when the doc has no heading.
  • New: import into any custom post type, and a Private status.
  • New: choose the featured image from the Media Library.
  • New: undo an import from the results screen (moves the posts to the Trash).
  • New: administrators can choose which roles may use DraftBridge.
  • New: a Site Health check for the server settings imports need.

1.1.6

  • New: footnotes and endnotes are imported, with numbered references in the text and the notes at the end of the post (WordPress Footnotes block in the block editor).
  • New: hover or tap a footnote number to read the note in a pop-up.
  • New: Word picture and table captions become real Image/Table block captions (figcaption), including captions in text boxes next to floating pictures.
  • Improved: floating (text-wrapped) pictures become their own Image block instead of sitting inside a paragraph.

1.1.5

  • Fix: version 1.1.4 could stop sites with a critical error because a file was missing from the release. Please update.

1.1.4

  • New: Send a Suggestion and Leave an Honest Review buttons on the DraftBridge screen.
  • New: an optional, dismissible reminder for admins asking for an honest review after 14 days and 3 imported docs. It appears on the Dashboard and DraftBridge screen, at most three times.

1.1.3

  • New plugin name: DraftBridge: From Doc/Docx to Blog Post.
  • The step-by-step guide link in the description is now a text link.
  • Tidier description layout.

1.1.2

  • The DraftBridge logo now appears at the top of the plugin screen.
  • Added a link to the step-by-step guide on the plugin screen and in the description.

1.1.1

  • New interface icons designed for DraftBridge.

1.1

  • New: Gutenberg block output, tables, nested and numbered lists.
  • New: SEO fields from the doc (Rank Math, Yoast SEO, SEOPress), FAQ schema, image links.
  • New: Preview, bulk import, categories, tags, author, status and scheduling.
  • Fixed: special characters in titles, bold text that was switched off, private Google Doc message, permissions for Authors and Contributors.

1.0

  • First release.
